title: Reviewing a Pipeline Before Production knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement correctly describes Reviewing a Pipeline Before Production?
options: Print all environment variables and event payloads to make the run easier to debug.
Run untrusted pull-request code in the same job that holds production credentials.
A pre-production review should verify passed checks, least-privilege access, protected environments, artifact provenance, health checks, rollback, and documentation.
Give every job write permission to avoid troubleshooting authorization errors.
questions.answer_key: A pre-production review should verify passed checks, least-privilege access, protected environments, artifact provenance, health checks, rollback, and documentation.
questions.explanation: This is the central behavior of reviewing a pipeline before production: A pre-production review should verify passed checks, least-privilege access, protected environments, artifact provenance, health checks, rollback, and documentation. Validate configuration and behavior against the current official reference before production use.

questions.prompt: A team is working with “Checking event coverage”. Which practice best fits this topic?
options: Match the event to the intended lifecycle, then test positive and negative branch/path/activity cases. Event payloads may be attacker-controlled, and scheduled jobs use UTC rather than a guaranteed exact start time.
Give every job write permission to avoid troubleshooting authorization errors.
Print all environment variables and event payloads to make the run easier to debug.
Run untrusted pull-request code in the same job that holds production credentials.
questions.answer_key: Match the event to the intended lifecycle, then test positive and negative branch/path/activity cases. Event payloads may be attacker-controlled, and scheduled jobs use UTC rather than a guaranteed exact start time.
questions.explanation: Checking event coverage: Match the event to the intended lifecycle, then test positive and negative branch/path/activity cases. Event payloads may be attacker-controlled, and scheduled jobs use UTC rather than a guaranteed exact start time. Apply the guidance to the actual event, runner, permissions, or artifact boundary and test the relevant case.

questions.prompt: How should a reviewer verify a change related to reviewing a pipeline before production?
options: Retry every failure without looking at the exit code or preserving evidence.
Publish the workflow to production before reviewing its triggers and permissions.
Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
Assume the workflow is correct as soon as the YAML file is committed.
questions.answer_key: Run a controlled test or static check, inspect the relevant job and step result, and compare the evidence with the stated acceptance criteria.
questions.explanation: Reliable verification uses observable evidence. For this lesson, consider: A pre-production review should verify passed checks, least-privilege access, protected environments, artifact provenance, health checks, rollback, and documentation. A syntax check alone cannot prove remote execution, permissions, or deployment behavior.
